questions.question: Explain who Leo Africanus was and how his book Description of Africa came to be written.
questions.expected_answer: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Wazzan, born in Granada about 1494 and raised in Fez, a scholar and diplomat who visited Timbuktu in about 1510. Captured by Christian pirates about 1518, he was given to Pope Leo X, baptised, and in Rome wrote in Italian a description of Africa based on his travels, finished about 1526 and published in 1550 by Ramusio.

questions.question: Evaluate Leo Africanus's account as a source on Timbuktu: give two strengths and two limitations.
questions.expected_answer: Strengths: he was an eyewitness; he was educated and understood Islamic society and trade; many details are confirmed by other sources. Limitations: written about 15 years later from memory; aimed at European readers in Rome, so possibly shaped for them; he was an outsider on a short visit with some biased attitudes; the editor changed the text; some details may be exaggerated.

questions.question: Explain why Timbuktu's location made it an important trade centre and name the main goods exchanged there.
questions.expected_answer: It lay at the southern edge of the Sahara near the Niger bend, where desert camel caravans met river boats. Camels could not survive in the humid south and boats could not cross the desert, so goods were exchanged there. Salt, cloth, copper, horses, paper and books came from the north; gold, kola nuts, grain, ivory and enslaved people came from the south.
